messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — high error rate (5xx) on /v1/generate in runtime-us-east-1. Current P95 latency spike + routing errors. Paging: @sofia (on-call)
sofia: on it. putting a quick triage channel here. can folks drop impact metrics and any recent deploys? :eyes:
arjun: seeing spike in 5xx starting ~10:03 UTC. rolling window shows 12% error at peak. no obvious infra autoscale events. no scheduled deploys flagged in deploy bot around that time.
maria: quick customer-impact note — a handful of enterprise tenants reported failed requests and timeouts. support has 8 open tickets referencing "generation failed". flagging for comms.
ben: copying some logs from the gateway (sanitized):
```
2026-03-21T10:02:58Z gateway-01 ERROR upstream request failed code=502 id=abcd1234 path=/v1/generate
2026-03-21T10:03:05Z gateway-02 ERROR connection reset by peer target=runtime-us-east-1-k8s
2026-03-21T10:03:15Z runtime-pod-7 WARN model-serve: kvcache miss spike, evictions=1423
```
sofia: thanks. hypothesis list (start): 1) runtime node OOM / kv cache thrash causing upstream resets 2) recent routing change to new model variant 3) network flaps in us-east AZ1. we should rule these out in parallel.
arjun: running `kubectl get pods -n runtime --selector=app=loader -o wide` now, paste output:
```
NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
loader-7c9fb8d6b-4t2xq     1/1     Running   0          4d    ip-10-0-2-45
loader-7c9fb8d6b-9kzrm     1/1     Running   0          4d    ip-10-0-3-12
serving-5d6b9f7-6mx2p      0/1     CrashLoop 3          10m   ip-10-0-2-45
```
arjun: ok one serving pod is CrashLooping, logs show repeated allocation failures and `CUDA out of memory` messages. copying snippet.
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256M.
Traceback ... model/lib/serve.py:line 412
```
sofia: that aligns with kvcache eviction spike. mitigation: 1) scale up serving replicas in us-east by +2 2) temporarily route heavy traffic to runtime-us-west while we stabilize 3) if a new model variant is causing higher memory, revert to previous variant.
claire: I can do the traffic routing change. doing a gradual shift via smart-router policy now: `route set --region us-east primary=false --weight 20%` then watch. will post results.
julian: I'm drafting a short status page update. suggestion copy:
"We are investigating elevated error rates impacting text generation in US-East. Some requests may return errors or experience timeouts. Our engineers are actively mitigating and will post updates every 30 minutes."
sofia: good. two comms items: who writes the public status (julian), who notifies enterprise customers (maria + ben), and when we post updates (every 30m). julian — can you push the first update in ~10 min? include impacted endpoints and ETA for next update.
julian: yes will post first update at 10:15 UTC. draft ready, ping me for edits.
maria: looping in account teams for the affected tenants, doing targeted emails with context and workaround (retry with exponential backoff). will include contacts for escalation.
arjun: mitigation step 1 executed: scaled serving replica set to +2. `kubectl scale deploy serving --replicas=5 -n runtime`. keeping watch. CPU/GPU usage dropping on newly started pods.
sofia: good. timeline so far (adding entries):
- 10:03 UTC: first 5xx alerts from gateway
- 10:04 UTC: incident-bot paged on-call
- 10:06 UTC: triage started, initial hypothesis (OOM / routing)
- 10:09 UTC: observed CrashLooping on serving pod; CUDA OOM in logs
- 10:12 UTC: scaled serving replicas +2
- 10:14 UTC: traffic routing change initiated (20% to us-west)
sofia: can everyone add any data points they have to this thread so we have a single canonical timeline for the post-incident RCA? please prefix entries with your initials.
ben: BEN: from net team — saw a short burst of packet drops on AZ1 between 10:01-10:05, but interface recovered. appears correlated with spike but not persistent.
arjun: ARJ: memory growth curve suggests a recent model variant 2026-03-20-variant-b increased peak memory usage by ~18% in canary. i opened a ticket on model-team to verify differences.
claire: CLA: router shift completed to 20% at 10:14, current error rate reduced from 12% -> 6% on us-east. continuing to increase weight if stable.
sofia: decision points: if error rate <3% after 30m and no new OOMs, we keep scaled replicas and roll forward; otherwise rollback model variant and revert routing. who wants to own rollback if needed?
arjun: I can own rollback. i'll coordinate with model-team and release bot. if we rollback, expect ~8-12 min for warmup.
maria: for customer comms: please share final severity classification. prelim SLO impact: many small-tier requests failed, enterprise tenants saw partial failures. classify currently as P2 (customer-impacting, degraded service).
sofia: noted. julian, include P2 in status, and indicate mitigation steps and ETA for next update. also tag on-call incident lead as contact.
julian: posted initial status page update: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1769054321 (draft). will update at 10:45 or sooner if major changes. ping me with copy edits.
incident-bot: automated note — please add postmortem labels within 72h: root-cause, mitigation, timeline, customer-impact, lessons. Reminder set.
sofia: handing off active incident coordination — i'm going offline at 10:30. handing to @arjun for live mitigation and to @julian for comms. arjun, julian — you're primary from 10:30-11:30. mark when you take over.
arjun: taking lead. will post running timeline updates and confirm rollback plan if OOMs persist. assigned incident-runner role.
julian: acknowledged, will continue status updates and escalate to SLs if needed. will sync with maria for targeted emails.
sofia: thanks team — great quick triage. please keep all technical notes and hypotheses in this thread for RCA build.
arjun: quick note: next steps captured, running `nvidia-smi dmon` on pods to watch mem usage and will paste summarized metrics in 10m.
ben: BEN: continuing to monitor network; no further sustained drops past 10:06.
claire: CLA: router increased to 50% at 10:24 — us-east error rate now ~2.8%. continuing to observe.
julian: posted second status update at 10:25 UTC: "Mitigation in progress; traffic rerouted; scaled up replicas. Next update 10:45 UTC or sooner." link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1769054321/update-2
sofia: last note before handoff — please capture all command outputs you run (kubectl, nv-smi, logs) into the incident doc. i'll join the RCA writeup later tonight. filing a follow-up meeting invite for post-incident review at 14:00 UTC.
arjun: ARJ: pasted nv-smi snapshots and heap profiles to the incident doc. continuing to watch."
